prompt: Complete the Square class so it extends the abstract Shape class: store the side length and implement the abstract area() method so the inherited describe() works.
explanation: An abstract class can mix abstract methods (area() has no body) with concrete ones (describe() is fully written). A concrete subclass like Square must implement every abstract method before it can be instantiated. When describe() runs, dynamic dispatch calls the subclass's area(), which is the template method pattern in miniature -- and every Square is-a Shape, as instanceof confirms.
hints: Declare private double side; and assign this.side = side; in the constructor.
area() just returns side * side. That single override satisfies the abstract method requirement.
You do not write describe() at all -- the inherited version calls area(), and at runtime that resolves to Square's implementation.
